classification.difficultyReason: The student finds stationary times from a factorising velocity, then compares displacement at the stationary time and both endpoints, and interprets the greatest magnitude as distance from the origin. In (b) the endpoint beats the turning points. The integer values keep it slightly easier than the surd version in p10-q4.

content.prompt: Each particle moves in a straight line, with displacement $x$ metres from the origin at time $t$ seconds.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A drone has displacement $x(t)=t^3-6t^2-15t$, $0\le t\le8$. What is the furthest the drone travels from the origin?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x'(t)&=3t^2-12t-15\\0&=3(t-5)(t+1)\\t&=5\qquad(0\le t\le8).\end{align*}$$
Compare displacement at the stationary time and the endpoints:
$$\begin{align*}x(0)&=0\\x(5)&=125-150-75=-100\\x(8)&=512-384-120=8.\end{align*}$$
Distance from the origin is $|x(t)|$, so the furthest distance is $100\text{ m}$ at $t=5$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A ball on a track has displacement $x(t)=t^3-9t^2+15t$, $0\le t\le8$. What is the furthest the ball travels from the origin?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x'(t)&=3t^2-18t+15\\0&=3(t-1)(t-5)\\t&=1\text{ or }5.\end{align*}$$
Compare displacement at the stationary times and the endpoints:
$$\begin{align*}x(0)&=0\\x(1)&=1-9+15=7\\x(5)&=125-225+75=-25\\x(8)&=512-576+120=56.\end{align*}$$
Distance from the origin is $|x(t)|$, so the furthest distance is $56\text{ m}$ at $t=8$.
